title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on this week's reliability incident: 5xx spikes and timeouts during peak traffic. Reviewed logs, root-cause hypotheses (bursting + KV cache cold-start + mis-sized concurrency), agreed on immediate mitigations and next steps: increase rate limit buckets, enable client-side exponential backoff, provision temporary burst capacity on Dedicated pool, and run focused benchmark with Redwood SE.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the incident we saw on Tuesday and agree next steps. We have Priya from infra here, and then from Acme I see Mark, Lisa, Evan, Sonia.
[00:18] Mark (Acme SRE): Hey. Yeah appreciate it. We had a big spike in 5xxs for about 12 minutes, about 3pm our time, lots of client retries and some timeouts. We surfaced a few customer-impacting failures.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks Mark. We pulled the logs - what we saw was concurrent request surges that caused queueing in the serving runtime; some requests hit the 30s client timeout. Also noticed a KV cache cold start on a couple of hosts which increased token generation time.
[00:52] Lisa (Backend Eng): We also saw a lot of 429/ rate limit messages in front of the Redwood API, then downstream 5xxs. So it's a mix? The client retried immediately and that made the spike worse.
[01:10] Alex (Redwood AE): Right, so two amplifying factors: client aggressive retries and a short burst capacity plus some cold caching behavior. Priya, do you want to walk through the timeline you built?
[01:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Sure. We instrumented traces - at t0 the load doubled, requests per second jumped ~4x for 10 minutes. The routing policy sent traffic to a small set of workers due to a temporary pod glitch. Those workers had cold KV cache and hit higher latencies, which cascaded into 500s. Then clients retried without exponential backoff so they overloaded the ingress.
[01:50] Mark (Acme SRE): Quick note - our client retry library is default settings, so it retried after 500ms then 1s; not exponential enough probably.
[02:00] Evan (Product): For context, this was during a campaign rollout so traffic pattern was unusual. We did not pre-warm.
[02:08] Sonia (Security): From a compliance perspective, any mitigation can't degrade audit logs or remove encryption - just checking we won't touch KMS or logs.
[02:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Absolutely - no changes to KMS or audit retention. Mitigations are config and routing level.
[02:25] Alex (Redwood AE): Ok let's talk mitigations: short-term we can increase your rate-limit bucket and enable a temporary Dedicated burst pool so traffic can be absorbed. Medium-term: tune client retry to exponential backoff with jitter and add a circuit breaker. Priya will propose specific settings.
[02:44] Priya (Redwood SE): Recommended immediate configs: client-side retry policy: max 3 attempts, base backoff 500ms, multiplier 2.0, jitter 0.2; server-side: raise concurrency cap by 40% for the next 48 hours, enable warm-starts on new workers and reduce idle eviction to keep KV cache hot. Also suggest enabling the prefix cache for common prompt prefixes.
[03:10] Lisa (Backend Eng): What's the risk of raising concurrency? We saw memory pressure before.
[03:17] Priya (Redwood SE): We'll size it conservatively - increase the per-worker concurrency on a small set first and monitor OOM metrics. If memory climbs, we can offload to a Dedicated burst pool.
[03:30] Mark (Acme SRE): For visibility, can you share the request traces and the trace ids for the 5xx spikes? Our on-call wants to correlate with infra graphs.
[03:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes. We'll export the traces and a zipped set of logs. We'll obfuscate PII but keep request ids.
[03:44] Alex (Redwood AE): We'll also open a support ticket for the incident and link it to your CRM deal so you have a single thread.
[03:50] Evan (Product): Any immediate code changes on our side besides retry settings?
[03:54] Lisa (Backend Eng): We could make requests idempotent where possible and add client-side rate limiting (token bucket) to smooth spikes.
[04:03] Alex (Redwood AE): Good call. Token bucket + exponential backoff is the recommended pattern.
[04:08] Priya (Redwood SE): Also wanted to call out model-level fallbacks; if a larger model causes latency we can route to a cheaper, faster variant automatically during high load. That trades cost for reliability.
[04:20] Sonia (Security): Any change to where data is stored if we switch models or routes? We need to ensure data residency and encryption remain per contract.
[04:27] Priya (Redwood SE): No change to storage or KMS; routing changes are internal and preserve your tenancy and encryption keys.
[04:33] Mark (Acme SRE): What about the rate limit header semantics - we saw a flurry of 429s but they came in batches. Is that a global limiter or per-route?
[04:42] Priya (Redwood SE): It's per-route by default but can be shaped per-client. For this POC we had a conservative per-route limit. We can bump the per-client burst token bucket to let short spikes through while still protecting shared capacity.
[04:58] Evan (Product): For the benchmark you suggested - what's the goal? Latency at p95 under load?
[05:03] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, run a stress test matching expected campaign traffic and measure p50/p95/p99, error rates, and queue lengths. We'll run it together so we can iterate on config.
[05:12] Lisa (Backend Eng): When can we do that? We need to coordinate internal deploys.
[05:15] Alex (Redwood AE): Let's propose Wed morning for the joint run. Priya can drive the test and we'll keep telemetry on.
[05:22] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll prepare a test plan: request pattern, token bucket settings, model variant, concurrency settings, and expected pass criteria.
[05:30] Mark (Acme SRE): One more question - you mentioned cache warmups. Is there a safe way to pre-warm KV cache for common keys?
[05:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, Redwood supports proactive KV pre-warming during deployments and we can hit the cache with representative prompts before traffic ramps. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity and keep caches warm.
[05:48] Sonia (Security): Are there any audit impacts of pre-warming? We just need to ensure logs show who ran it.
[05:54] Priya (Redwood SE): Pre-warm actions will be logged as part of the deployment runbook; we'll include those entries in the export.
[06:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Ok let's record concrete action items and next steps.
[06:05] Mark (Acme SRE): Quick note - transcription may be a little rough, some names might be off in the exported text.
[06:12] Alex (Redwood AE): Good point.
[06:15] [RECAPPING ACTIONS] Alex (Redwood AE): Priya will share logs/traces and a test plan by EOD tomorrow; Acme will update client retry settings and client token-bucket by end of day Friday; Redwood will provision temporary burst capacity and open a support ticket; we'll do a joint stress test Wednesday morning.
[06:40] Evan (Product): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:45] Alex (Redwood AE): Thanks - we'll follow up in email with links and the support ticket id.
[06:50] END
